note: Adapted from entry 92 of Roonwal & Chhotani (1997), originally in English. The original gives the antennal segment counts of the soldier and the worker as “12–15” and “14–15” respectively; in the worker the OCR reads “T4-15”, which has been read as 14–15 from the context. The diagnostic characters follow the alate and soldier keys of that work (p. 571–572); in the keys the pronotal width is given as 0.95–1.10 mm, slightly different from the 0.95–1.00 mm of the species description, and each figure is entered here as printed. The synonymy list, literature citations, figure numbers, type-specimen records and distribution records have been omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head length to mandibular base 2.15–2.45, width 1.40–1.55 mm; antennae relatively slender with segment 2 small; ratio of postmental waist width to maximum width 0.47–0.55; in the comparable beesoni the antennae are stouter and segment 2 larger, that ratio being 0.37–0.40. Alate (darker and smaller): antennae 16–17-segmented, head length to mandibular base 1.00–1.13, width 1.25–1.30 mm, fore wing length 8.0–9.10 mm; in fletcheri the antennae are 18–19-segmented, head length 1.18–1.24, width 1.45–1.55 mm, fore wing length 9.95–10.80 mm.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule, pronotum, abdominal tergites and the anterior margin of the wings dark brown; antennae, postclypeus, labrum and mandibular base yellowish brown. Head with moderate hair, body densely hairy. Body length with wings 9.4–10.7 mm. Head capsule nearly square (width 1.25–1.30, length to mandibular base 1.00–1.13 mm); sides nearly rounded; posterior margin broadly rounded; Y suture indistinct. Fontanelle minute, circular, situated slightly behind the middle of the head. Eyes rather large, black, nearly circular (long diameter 0.33–0.45, short diameter 0.29–0.40 mm). Ocelli small, oval (long diameter 0.13–0.15, short diameter 0.08–0.10 mm), 0.04–0.05 mm from the eye (about half their short diameter). Antennae 16–17-segmented; segment 2 longer than segment 3, segment 4 (in a 16-segmented antenna) or segment 3 (in a 17-segmented antenna) shortest. Postclypeus narrow, nearly rectangular (length less than half its width), with a few hairs; anteclypeus narrow, transparent, bare, with a median concavity on the anterior margin. Mandibles of the Stylotermes type. Pronotum flat, trapezoidal, much wider than long (width 0.95–1.00, length 0.50–0.60 mm); narrower than the head width including the eyes; anterior margin nearly straight with a median concavity, posterior margin nearly straight, with or without a median concavity. Legs rather long; femora inflated; tibiae slender, tibial spurs 3:2:2; tarsi 3-segmented. Wings transparent, the anterior margin dark. Fore wing slightly longer than the hind wing, length 8.00–9.10 mm; costa and radius thick and nearly parallel, closely appressed; media weak, unbranched, central; cubitus weak, with 19–21 branches. Hind wing as the fore wing, except that the media arises from the radius outside the wing scale. Abdomen elongate; cerci 2-segmented; abdominal styli absent.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule generally reddish brown, the anterior part of the head, the antennae and the mandibular base paler; labrum, pronotum and legs yellowish brown; body yellow. Head sparsely hairy, body moderately hairy. Body length 6.55–7.50 mm. Head capsule rectangular, much longer than wide (length to mandibular base 2.15–2.45, width 1.40–1.55 mm), the sides nearly parallel, converging slightly posteriorly to the broadly rounded posterior margin; the lateral arms of the Y suture visible, the posterior arm indistinct. Fontanelle minute, situated in the anterior 1/3 of the head. Eyes small, white, near the antennal socket. Ocelli minute, dot-like, about one long eye diameter from the eye. Antennae 12–15-segmented; segment 2 shortest, segment 3 longer than segment 4, segments 4, 5 and 6 subequal in length. Postclypeus with a few hairs, nearly rectangular, indistinctly delimited from the frontal area; anteclypeus white, bare. Labrum dome-shaped, wider than long, with several long hairs on the surface and on the rounded anterior margin. Mandibles reddish brown at the base and otherwise nearly black; stout, sabre-shaped, slightly incurved at the apex, rather short (length 1.25–1.38 mm, mandible length/head length ratio 0.53–0.63). Inner margin of the left mandible smooth, with only a minute serration at the base; inner margin of the right mandible also smooth, but with a large knob-like process at the base. Postmentum club-shaped, the anterior part (the club) bilobed and widest, narrowing posteriorly into a slender waist (length 1.45–1.70, maximum width 0.48–0.60, waist width 0.25–0.33 mm). Pronotum nearly trapezoidal, wider than long (width 1.10–1.18, length 0.70–0.80 mm), slightly narrower than the head; anterior margin deeply concave with broadly rounded anterolateral corners; the sides converging posteriorly to the nearly straight posterior margin. Legs long, femora inflated, tibiae slender, tibial spurs 3:2:2; tarsi 3-segmented. Abdomen elongate; cerci 2-segmented.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule, antennae, postclypeus and labrum white-yellow to yellow; pronotum paler; anteclypeus pale yellowish white; legs and abdomen white. Head sparsely hairy, body more hairy. Body length 4.20–5.30 mm. Head capsule nearly circular, slightly wider than long (length to mandibular base 1.05–1.20, width 1.18–1.30 mm); Y suture faintly visible. Fontanelle minute. Eyes oval, small, reduced. Antennae 14–15-segmented; segment 4 shortest. Postclypeus slightly inflated, deeper than the frontal area; anterior margin concave; a few hairs near the margin and on the surface. Anteclypeus trapezoidal, bare. Labrum dome-shaped, wider than long; anterior margin slightly convex, with a few hairs near the margin and on the surface. Mandibles of the Stylotermes type. Pronotum trapezoidal, wider than long (width 0.90–1.05, length 0.55–0.65 mm), narrower than the head; anterior margin concave without a median notch, posterior margin slightly convex, with or without a median concavity. Legs and abdomen as in the soldier.
